title: "Install, in order"
description: "What I install on a Windows 11 machine for R in VS Code: VS Code, rig and R, Python and radian, Rtools, the R packages, Quarto."
date-format: long
date-modified: last-modified
---

Everything can be done from PowerShell with [`winget`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/package-manager/winget/), which comes with Windows 11.

Install R before Rtools and the R packages, and Python before radian. After changing `PATH`, programs only see the change when they are started again (see [step 9](#restart-vs-code-and-test)).

## Versions I use

| Software | Version |
|---|---|
| VS Code | 1.134 |
| rig | 0.11.1 |
| R | 4.6.2 (also used: 4.5.x) |
| Python | 3.12.10 |
| radian / rchitect | 0.7.1 / 0.5.2 |
| Rtools | 4.5 |
| Quarto | 1.11.9 |
| RStudio | 2026.10.1 |
| vscode-R extension | 3.3 |

## 1. VS Code

```powershell
winget install Microsoft.VisualStudioCode
```

Or download it from <https://code.visualstudio.com/Download> (the *User Installer* is fine). Then turn on **Settings Sync** (the account icon, bottom left) and sign in. On a machine that already has a synced set-up, this brings back the profiles, settings, keybindings, snippets, tasks and extensions. Read [Profiles and Settings Sync](profiles_sync.qmd) first: two R settings do not sync unless you tell VS Code to sync them.

## 2. rig, then R

[rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig) installs and switches R versions. It keeps the set-up free of machine-specific paths: VS Code and radian use "the `R` on `PATH`", and rig decides which version that is.

```powershell
winget install Posit.rig
```

Open a new terminal (so it sees rig on `PATH`), then:

```powershell
rig add release          # the current R release; accept the UAC prompt
rig default 4.6.2        # the version used everywhere; `rig list` shows what is installed
rig system make-links    # version-named shortcuts: R-4.6.2, R-4.5.1, ...
rig system fix-r-alias   # make `R` start R in PowerShell
```

- `rig add release` looks stuck with no output when it is waiting for the UAC prompt, which can be hidden behind other windows.
- `rig add 4.5.1` (or `rig add 4.5`) installs an older version next to it.
- In PowerShell, `R` is a built-in alias for `Invoke-History`. `rig system fix-r-alias` removes that alias in your PowerShell profile (see [Outside VS Code](outside_vscode.qmd#powershell)).
- rig puts its shortcuts (`R.exe`, `Rscript.exe`, `R-4.6.2.exe`, ...) in `C:\Program Files\R\bin`, which must be on `PATH`. Do not also add a version folder such as `C:\Program Files\R\R-x.y.z\bin` to `PATH`, and do not set `R_HOME`: both pin one version and override rig (see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#radian-or-vs-code-starts-an-old-r-version)).
- rig does not install Rtools (step 6).

## 3. RStudio (optional)

```powershell
winget install Posit.RStudio
```

rig registers its R versions with RStudio, so there is nothing else to set up. Its bundled pandoc is also used by my `.Rprofile` ([Outside VS Code](outside_vscode.qmd#rprofile)).

## 4. Python (python.org build)

radian is a Python program, so it needs Python. I use Python 3.12, the python.org build, not the Microsoft Store one:

```powershell
winget install Python.Python.3.12 --override "/quiet InstallAllUsers=0 PrependPath=1 Include_launcher=1 Include_test=0"
```

- `PrependPath=1` puts `Python312\` and `Python312\Scripts\` on your user `PATH`. `Scripts\` is where `radian.exe` will be.
- If another Python is installed (a Store one, or 3.13+), 3.12 must come first on `PATH`. Check in a new terminal: `python --version` and `Get-Command radian` must both point to `Python312`.

## 5. radian

[radian](https://github.com/randy3k/radian) is a better R console: syntax highlighting, multi-line editing, and autocompletion.

```powershell
python -m pip install -U radian
radian --version   # shows the radian, R and Python versions it uses
```

`radian --version` should report the R version you set with `rig default`. If it shows another one, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#radian-or-vs-code-starts-an-old-r-version).

If the install fails while compiling, install the [Microsoft C++ Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/).

## 6. Rtools

[Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) compiles R packages from source (needed for GitHub packages such as vscDebugger, and for your own packages).

```powershell
winget install RProject.Rtools
```

- Rtools 4.5 covers R 4.5.0 and later, including 4.6.x. There is no separate Rtools 4.6.
- Check in R: `pkgbuild::has_build_tools()` should be `TRUE`, and `Sys.which("make")` should point into `C:\rtools45\`.

## 7. The R packages

These are needed once per R version: each R version has its own package library, and a new version starts empty.

```r
install.packages(c("languageserver", "remotes", "httpgd", "devtools", "lintr", "styler", "btw"))
remotes::install_github("ManuelHentschel/vscDebugger")
```

| Package | Why |
|---|---|
| `languageserver` | Autocompletion, go to definition, hover help and diagnostics in VS Code. |
| `vscDebugger` | The R debugger behind the R Debugger extension. Only on GitHub, so it needs Rtools. |
| `httpgd` | The plot viewer. VS Code shows plots from it (`r.plot.backend: "httpgd"`). |
| `devtools` | Package development; brings `usethis` (used by the [scratch project task](snippets_tasks.qmd#r-new-scratch-project)). |
| `lintr` | Linting in the editor. Needs lintr 3.3.0-1 or newer. |
| `styler` | Formatting, used by `languageserver` for "Format Document". |
| `btw` | Exposes the R session to coding assistants (MCP). My `.Rprofile` starts it when installed. Optional. |

## 8. Quarto

```powershell
winget install Posit.Quarto
```

This installs Quarto for all users in `C:\Program Files\Quarto`.

## 9. Restart VS Code and test {#restart-vs-code-and-test}

**Quit every VS Code window and start it again.** VS Code and all its terminals keep the `PATH` they were started with, and *Developer: Reload Window* does not refresh it.

Then:

1. Open an R file, then *Command Palette* → **Terminal: Create New Terminal**. With the [settings](settings.qmd) in place, it opens radian (the default terminal profile is "R Terminal").
2. Run `plot(1:10)`. The plot opens in the httpgd viewer beside the editor.
3. Run `R.version.string`. It shows rig's default version.

If something fails, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).

The rest of the environment comes from the profile: [settings](settings.qmd), [keybindings](keybindings.qmd), [extensions](extensions.qmd), [snippets and tasks](snippets_tasks.qmd), plus a few files [outside VS Code](outside_vscode.qmd). The [overview](index.qmd#rebuild-from-scratch) has the whole rebuild as one checklist.
